# dsh-skin-tomorrow-night-blue
**Tomorrow Night Blue skin for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI.**
English | 中文

One skin, the whole interface: the classic deep-blue **Tomorrow Night Blue**
palette (Chris Kempson'

s Tomorrow Theme)
mapped onto DSH's design tokens and code-highlighting colors — canvas, sidebar,
pa

nels, menus, buttons, conversation bubbles, markdown, diffs, scrollbars, focus
ring, and syntax high
lighting in code blocks.
> Unofficial community skin. Not affiliated with DeepSeek.
## Install

`desktop` for the DSH D

DSH applies profile changes live; if the palette does not appear immediately,
restart DSH once (the
browser half loads with the app shell).
## What it does

- **113 `--dsw-alias-*` design tokens** — application canvas, raised layers,
overlays, borders, labe

ls, brand/link/button colors, interactive and state
colors, markdown, diff, file-diff, scrollbar, fo

cus ring, toast, tooltip, menu
and product-specific surfaces (sidebar, bubble, composer, selector, t

ips).
- **11 Shiki syntax roles** — comments, keywords, strings, numbers/constants,
functions, param

eters, punctuation and links in fenced code blocks match the
theme instead of keeping the stock Shik

i palette.
- **First paint is already blue** — the host half injects the same declarations
into ever

y served `index.html` through the webserver's structured
`index-inject` rows, so a browser page does

not flash the default palette
while its scripts load.
- **No dependencies, no network, no settings

namespace** — one stylesheet and
one token layer; disable or remove the bundle to get the stock look

ace** — one stylesheet and
one token layer; disable or remove the bundle to get the stock look back.
## Palette

| Background | `#002451` | | Red | `#FF9DA4` |
| Current line / raised surface | `#00346E` | | Orang

e | `#FFC58F` |
| Selection / nested surface | `#003F8E` | | Yellow | `#FFEEAD` |
| Foreground | `#F

FFFFF` | | Green | `#D1F1A9` |
| Comment | `#7285B7` | | Aqua | `#99FFFF` |
| | | | Blue | `#BBDAFF`

|
| | | | Purple | `#EBBBFF` |

Tomorrow Night Blue has no official light counterpart, so the skin keeps this
palette in both appear

ance modes and aligns the appearance setting to dark on
first use.
## How it works

This is a two-half DSH plugin (all standard DSH plugin metadata, no custom
wiring):
| Half | File | Role |
| Host | `index.js` | Pushes one structured `style` row into `webserver/index-inject` so served page

s paint the skin before scripts run. |
| Client | `lib/client.js` | Appends one `<style>` element wi
th the token + Shiki declarations and registers it with the app's `__ModuleLoader__` bundle format.
h the token + Shiki declarations and registers it with the app's `__ModuleLoader__` bundle format. |

`src/palette.mjs` is the single source of truth: a 15-anchor palette expanded
into the `--dsw-alias-

*` surface. `build-client.mjs` serializes that derivation
into the browser bundle; `verify.mjs` re-d

erives it offline and exercises both
halves against stubs.

The declarations are `!important` on purpose: DSH's layout presenter writes the
composed alias token

s as **inline** custom properties on `<body>`, and only an
important stylesheet declaration outranks

inline style. A fixed skin must win
that cascade; a theme that wants to stay configurable should us

e the
`ctx.theme.overrideTokens` layer instead.
## Compatibility

- DSH Web GUI **0.2.x** (developed and tested against `0.2.2-rc.1`, DSH
Desktop profile; the same cl

ient bundle serves `dsh --profile web`).
- Node.js `>=20` for the build/verify scripts (runtime need

s no build).
- While enabled, the skin's `!important` layer takes precedence over token
layers from

other skin plugins (for example `dsh-opencode-palette`). Disable
this bundle to hand the cascade bac

plugins (for example `dsh-opencode-palette`). Disable
this bundle to hand the cascade back to them.
### Known limitations

- The skin overrides **alias tokens** (plus the Shiki syntax roles). A few
auxiliary surfaces in DSH

are painted from design-system **static** tokens
(for example some file-change/diff card headers ke

ep a neutral dark fill) and
therefore stay as the stock theme draws them — the same boundary every
t

oken-layer skin works within.
- Tomorrow Night Blue is a dark palette; the skin keeps it under both
appearance modes by design.
## Disable / uninstall

- **Settings → Plugins** → turn off or remove `dsh-skin-tomorrow-night-blue`.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --p
rofile <profile> remove dsh-skin-tomorrow-night-blue`
## Development

`verify.mjs` requires no DSH runtime: it derives the token surface, calls the
host `apply` with a fa

ke context and a captured injection table, then loads the
built bundle through the real `window.__Mo

duleLoader__` factory shape against a
DOM stub.
